matched-betting.title: Matched betting: extracting profit from welcome bonuses
matched-betting.metaTitle: Matched betting – how to exploit bookmaker bonuses
matched-betting.description: Matched betting explained: how to use welcome bonuses and free bets at licensed bookmakers to lock in a profit, and how it differs from sure bets.
matched-betting.intro: Matched betting is a technique for converting bookmakers' bonuses and free bets into real cash. By backing and laying the same event, you cover all outcomes so the result doesn't matter – what remains is a guaranteed profit from the bonus.

blocks.text: How matched betting works

When you claim a free bet or bonus, you place it on one outcome at a bookmaker and lay (bet against) the same outcome at a betting exchange or back the opposite result with another bookmaker. Because the free bet stakes nothing of your own money, you lock in most of its face value as profit regardless of which side wins.
Bonus terms and restrictions

Welcome bonuses carry different terms depending on the bookmaker and the country in which you're betting. Some regulated markets cap bonus amounts and limit wagering requirements to protect consumers. Always read the specific terms and conditions before you accept any offer.

items: Check the minimum odds required to unlock the bonus – many bookmakers set a floor of 1.80 or higher.
Note the expiry period so your bonus or free bet doesn't lapse unused.
Consider using sure bets (arbitrage bets) to meet turnover requirements with minimal risk.

blocks.text: Combining matched betting with sure bets

Sure bets are ideal for clearing bonus wagering requirements because you're not staking real money on a single outcome. Once you've met the rollover, you can carry on finding arbitrage opportunities without relying on promotions.

faq.q: Is matched betting legal?
faq.a: Yes. Exploiting bonuses within the bookmaker's published terms is perfectly legal. However, bookmakers reserve the right to withdraw offers or limit accounts if they believe you are not betting in the spirit of their promotions or if you breach the terms.

faq.q: How much are typical welcome bonuses worth?
faq.a: Bonus values and wagering requirements vary by bookmaker and jurisdiction. In some regulated markets, welcome offers may be capped – for instance at £1,000 or €1,000 with a maximum rollover of ten times the bonus. Always check the current terms at the bookmaker you choose and confirm that it holds a valid licence in your country.

er-surebets-lovligt.title: Are surebets legal? Rules and tax considerations
er-surebets-lovligt.metaTitle: Are surebets legal? Rules, tax and bookmaker terms
er-surebets-lovligt.description: Is it legal to place surebets, and do you have to pay tax on winnings? Here are the rules and what bookmakers can do about arbitrage betting.
er-surebets-lovligt.intro: The short answer is yes. Placing surebets is legal in most jurisdictions. You are simply placing ordinary bets with licensed bookmakers and comparing odds to find the best value – nothing about this process is illegal.

blocks.text: What can bookmakers do?

Although surebets are legal, bookmakers do not welcome customers who consistently place guaranteed-profit bets. In their terms and conditions, they reserve the right to reduce maximum stakes, limit markets or restrict accounts. However, they must always return your deposited funds and pay out any valid winnings.
Do you have to pay tax on winnings?

Tax treatment of betting winnings varies by country. In many regulated markets, winnings from operators licensed by your national gambling regulator are tax-free for the player. If you use offshore or unlicensed operators, your winnings may be taxable. Check the tax rules where you live, or consult your local tax authority if you are unsure about your situation.
Stick to bookmakers licensed by your national regulator. This typically offers tax advantages and consumer protection from your gambling authority.
Responsible gambling

Even with surebets, it is important to maintain control over your gambling. Set deposit limits, and use your country's self-exclusion register if you need a break. If you need support, contact a recognised gambling helpline in your region.

faq.q: Can a bookmaker refuse to pay out winnings from a surebet?
faq.a: A bookmaker must pay out valid winnings. It can void a bet if there was an obvious error in the odds, and it can restrict the account going forward.

faq.q: Do I have to pay tax on surebet winnings?
faq.a: It depends on your country. In many regulated markets, winnings from licensed operators are tax-free for the player. Check the tax rules where you live.

undgaa-begraensning.title: How to avoid bookmaker account limits and gubbing
undgaa-begraensning.metaTitle: Avoid bookmaker limits – tips for arbers & value bettors
undgaa-begraensning.description: Bookmakers limit accounts that win consistently. Learn the key tactics to keep your accounts active longer when placing arbitrage bets and value bets.
undgaa-begraensning.intro: The biggest challenge with arbitrage betting and value betting isn't finding the opportunities – it's keeping your accounts open. Bookmakers monitor betting patterns closely, and accounts that consistently win are often restricted or 'gubbed'. With a few smart habits, you can extend the lifespan of your accounts significantly.

blocks.text: Why do bookmakers limit accounts?

Bookmakers profit from their margin. A customer who consistently beats the market by exploiting arbs or finding value bets costs them money. Their risk-management systems flag patterns such as unusual stake amounts, bets on obscure markets, wagers placed immediately after odds shifts, and accounts that rarely bet on recreational markets.
Best practices to avoid account limits

items: Round your stakes – for example, £50 or €100 instead of £47.83 or €93.42.
Avoid the highest-profit sure bets and arbs. These often result from pricing errors and draw immediate attention.
Place occasional bets on mainstream events and popular markets (football accumulators, horse racing, in-play tennis).
Don't withdraw winnings immediately after each winning bet. Leave funds in your account and withdraw less frequently.
Rotate your activity across multiple bookmakers rather than hammering the same few repeatedly.

blocks.text: Track your bets in the accounts section so you can see which bookmakers you're using most heavily and spread your activity more evenly across your portfolio.
What to do if you get limited

A limited account isn't useless. You can often still use it for promotional offers, matched betting or smaller stakes. Always maintain more accounts than you strictly need, so you can continue operating smoothly even if one bookmaker reduces your limits or closes your account.

faq.q: Can a bookmaker close your account completely?
faq.a: Licensed bookmakers can close accounts according to their terms and conditions, but they are legally required to pay out any remaining balance and outstanding winnings.

faq.q: How long before you typically get gubbed or limited?
faq.a: It varies considerably between bookmakers and depends on your betting behaviour. Some restrict accounts after a few weeks of consistent winning, others after several months of activity. Sharper bookmakers tend to act more quickly.

undgaa-begraensning.ctaLabel: Track your bets in the accounts

surebet-beregner.title: Surebet calculator: how to distribute your stake correctly
surebet-beregner.metaTitle: Surebet calculator – distribute stake and see profit
surebet-beregner.description: See the formula behind a surebet calculator and learn to distribute your stake across two or three outcomes for guaranteed equal payout on any result.
surebet-beregner.intro: A surebet calculator tells you how much to stake on each outcome so the payout is identical regardless of how the event ends. Here's the formula so you understand what the calculator does.

blocks.text: The formula

First add the inverse odds together: 1/odds A + 1/odds B (+ 1/odds C for three outcomes). Call the sum S. The stake on each outcome is then the total stake times 1/odds for that outcome, divided by S.

blocks.title: Example: football with three outcomes (1X2), total stake £1,000
blocks.note: The sum is above 1, so here you'll lose around 2.5% regardless of the outcome. The calculator shows this immediately, so you avoid poor combinations.

blocks.text: Rounding your stakes
Stakes like £493.98 can make bookmakers notice you're using a calculator. Round to whole pounds or fifty pence. It costs a bit of profit but makes your bets look more natural.
In the BetTrackerAI calculator you can adjust odds directly and see how the distribution and profit change instantly.

faq.q: Does the calculator work with three outcomes too?
faq.a: Yes. The formula is the same. You just add the third inverse odds into the sum and distribute the stake across three bets.

faq.q: Is the calculator free?
faq.a: Yes. The calculator on BetTrackerAI can be used for free.

odds-beregner.title: How to use an odds calculator
odds-beregner.metaTitle: Odds calculator – convert odds to probability and winnings
odds-beregner.description: Learn to convert decimal odds to probability, calculate your potential winnings, and find the bookmaker's margin with an odds calculator.
odds-beregner.intro: An odds calculator turns odds into something you can use: how much you'll win, how likely the bookmaker thinks the outcome is, and how much the bookmaker is taking. Here are the three calculations you need to know.

blocks.text: 1. Potential winnings
With decimal odds, which most online bookmakers use, the payout is stake multiplied by odds. The profit is the payout minus the stake.
2. Implied probability
The probability the bookmaker is working with is 1 divided by the odds. Odds of 2.50 equals 40%. If you believe the chance is higher, it's a value bet.
3. Bookmaker margin

Add up the implied probabilities for all outcomes. The total is over 100%, and the excess is the bookmaker margin. If the total is under 100% across different bookmakers, you have a surebet (also known as an arbitrage bet).

blocks.title: Tennis: odds of 1.85 and 1.95 at the same bookmaker
blocks.note: The lower the margin, the better odds you get as a punter.

blocks.text: Our free sure bet calculator does all three calculations for you and distributes the stake across multiple outcomes.

faq.q: How do you convert odds to a percentage?
faq.a: Divide 1 by the odds and multiply by 100. Odds of 2.00 equals 50%, and odds of 4.00 equals 25%.

faq.q: What's the difference between decimal odds and fractional odds?
faq.a: Decimal odds show the total payout per unit staked, e.g. 2.50. Fractional odds, such as 3/2, show only the profit. Most online bookmakers use decimal odds, though fractional odds remain common in the UK and Ireland.

value-betting-vs-surebets.title: Value betting vs surebets: what's the difference?
value-betting-vs-surebets.metaTitle: Value betting vs surebets – differences, risk & profit
value-betting-vs-surebets.description: Value betting and surebets both exploit mispriced odds but work differently. Compare risk, profit potential and which strategy suits your betting style.
value-betting-vs-surebets.intro: Both value betting and surebets exploit bookmakers' pricing errors. The key difference: surebets lock in guaranteed profit instantly, whilst value betting delivers profit over a large sample of bets.

blocks.text: What is value betting?

A value bet is a wager where the odds are higher than the true probability suggests. If a match is genuinely 50/50 and a bookmaker offers odds of 2.20, that's a value bet. You only bet on one outcome and can lose individual bets, but over time the edge delivers profit.
What is a surebet?
With a surebet (arbitrage bet) you back all outcomes across different bookmakers so you win regardless of the result. The profit per bet is smaller, but it's guaranteed on every trade.

blocks.title: Comparison
rows: Surebets: several · Value: one or more

blocks.text: Which strategy suits you?

items: Choose surebets if you want stable profit without large swings or drawdowns.
Choose value betting if you can tolerate losing runs and have a large enough bankroll to ride out variance.
Many combine both: surebets for steady income and value bets to maximise long-term edge.

blocks.text: If you're starting out, begin with surebets. You'll learn how bookmakers operate without risking large losses.

faq.q: Is value betting more profitable than surebets?
faq.a: Value betting can deliver higher profit over the long term, but with far greater variance. Surebets offer smaller, more stable profit on every bet.

faq.q: Do bookmakers limit your account with value betting too?
faq.a: Yes. Bookmakers limit winning customers regardless of strategy, though value betting can be slightly harder to detect because you also place losing bets.

bedste-bookmakere-til-surebets.title: Best bookmakers for surebets
bedste-bookmakere-til-surebets.description: Which bookmakers should you use for surebets? See what makes a good arbitrage betting bookmaker and how to build your portfolio of accounts.
bedste-bookmakere-til-surebets.intro: There isn't one single bookmaker that's best for surebets. Arbitrage betting opportunities arise between bookmakers, so the most important thing is to have accounts with several operators using different odds providers and different approaches to the market.

blocks.text: Why multiple bookmakers give you more surebets

Many bookmakers use the same odds platform and therefore have near-identical prices. Surebets most often arise between bookmakers that set odds in their own different ways. If you only have accounts with bookmakers on the same platform, you'll see far fewer arbitrage betting opportunities.
What to look for

items: Licensed by your national gambling regulator, so you're protected and can verify the tax treatment of your winnings.
Fast deposits and withdrawals, so you can move money where it's needed.
Wide range of sports and markets, especially tennis, football and basketball.
Competitive odds and low bookmaker margin on popular markets.
A welcome bonus with reasonable terms that you can clear using surebets.

blocks.text: How to build your bookmaker portfolio

Start with five to eight licensed bookmakers spread across different platforms. This gives you a good range of opportunities without having to manage too many balances. Once you've got the routine down, you can expand with more.
In BetTrackerAI you can select exactly which bookmakers you have accounts with, so you only see surebets you can actually place.
Bookmakers with their own odds are worth their weight in gold

Bookmakers that set their own odds instead of buying them often react more slowly or differently to news. This is precisely where the price differences arise. On the flip side, they're also often the quickest to limit winning accounts through gubbing.

faq.q: How many bookmakers do I need for surebets?
faq.a: A good starting point is five to eight regulated bookmakers. The more different odds platforms you cover, the more surebets you'll have access to.

faq.q: Can I use unlicensed bookmakers for arbitrage betting?
faq.a: It's not recommended. Bookmakers without a licence in your jurisdiction may be blocked, and winnings from them may be subject to different tax treatment or lack regulatory protection. Always check the rules where you live.

skat-paa-spillegevinster.title: Tax on gambling winnings – international betting guide
skat-paa-spillegevinster.metaTitle: Tax on Gambling Winnings – What You Need to Know
skat-paa-spillegevinster.description: Do you need to pay tax on betting winnings and surebets? Learn how tax rules work for licensed and offshore bookmakers, and what to document.
skat-paa-spillegevinster.intro: In many regulated markets, the answer is straightforward: winnings from licensed bookmakers are tax-free for the player. The bookmaker pays duty to the state, not you. But the rules depend on where you live and where you bet.

blocks.text: Licensed bookmakers: typically tax-free

When you bet with a provider licensed by your national gambling regulator, the provider usually pays gambling duty on their revenue. Your winnings are therefore generally tax-free, and in most cases you don't need to report them to your tax authority. Always check the rules where you live.
Offshore bookmakers without a local licence

If you bet with providers that do not hold a licence in your jurisdiction, the winnings may be taxable. The rules depend on factors such as whether the provider holds a licence in another country and your own tax residence. This is one reason why it's often simpler to stick with regulated bookmakers.
Does this apply to surebets too?

Yes. For tax purposes, a surebet is simply two or three ordinary bets. Winnings from licensed bookmakers are generally tax-free, whether you're placing sure bets, value bets or standard bets. The same principles apply.
Keep a record of your bets. It makes it easy to document where the money comes from if your bank asks.
Professional gambling

If betting is your main occupation on a substantial scale, different rules may apply in certain jurisdictions. If you're unsure about your own situation, contact your local tax authority or a qualified accountant.

faq.q: Do I need to pay tax on winnings from licensed bookmakers?
faq.a: In most regulated markets, no. Winnings from locally licensed providers are typically tax-free for the player. Check the tax rules where you live.

faq.q: How can I see if a bookmaker is licensed in my country?
faq.a: Your national gambling regulator will have a list of approved providers on its website, and licensed bookmakers usually display the regulator's logo on their site.

skat-paa-spillegevinster.ctaLabel: Read about the rules for surebets

bankroll-management.title: Bankroll management for arbitrage betting and sports betting
bankroll-management.metaTitle: Bankroll management for arbitrage betting – fund control
bankroll-management.description: How to split your bankroll across bookmakers, stake the right amount per arb, and ensure capital is available when opportunities appear.
bankroll-management.intro: Your bankroll is the capital you've set aside for betting. With arbitrage betting, bankroll management is less about avoiding losses and more about having funds in the right place when an arb appears.

blocks.text: Set a fixed bankroll
Decide on an amount you can afford to lose and keep it separate from your other money. Only use that amount for betting, and don't add more funds just because a single bet went wrong.
Distribute funds between bookmakers

An arb requires stakes at two or three bookmakers simultaneously. Therefore, distribute your bankroll so each bookmaker has enough for at least a couple of bets. Bookmakers that frequently feature in arbs should receive slightly more.

blocks.title: Example: £10,000 bankroll distributed across 6 bookmakers
blocks.note: With this distribution, you can cover several arbs in a row before needing to move money around.

blocks.text: How much should you stake per arb?

A good rule of thumb is 5–10% of your total bankroll per arb. That's high compared to regular betting, but the risk is also far lower. Reduce your stakes if the odds are unstable or if you're new to arbing.
Keep records of all bets. This lets you see which bookmakers are tying up the most funds, so you can distribute your bankroll better.
Move winnings regularly
After a period, funds accumulate with some bookmakers and run short with others. Withdraw from those with too much and deposit with those with too little, for example once a week.

faq.q: How large a bankroll do I need to start arbitrage betting?
faq.a: You can start with a couple of thousand in your currency, but £5,000–10,000 (or equivalent) makes it easier to have sufficient funds with multiple bookmakers at once.

faq.q: Can you lose money on arbitrage bets?
faq.a: It can happen if odds change before you place the second bet, or if a bet is voided. Good bankroll management limits the damage.

arbitrage-betting.title: Arbitrage betting: the complete guide
arbitrage-betting.metaTitle: Arbitrage betting guide – how to place surebets profitably
arbitrage-betting.description: Arbitrage betting explained: what it is, how to get started, which bookmakers to use, and how to manage your bankroll effectively.
arbitrage-betting.intro: Arbitrage betting is the practice of placing surebets. The idea is the same as in financial markets: you exploit a price difference between two markets and lock in a profit before the market corrects itself.

blocks.text: How to get started

items: Open accounts with several licensed bookmakers. The more accounts, the more opportunities.
Deposit a starting bankroll and distribute it across the bookmakers.
Use a scanner to find opportunities in real time instead of comparing odds manually.
Use a sure bet calculator so your stake is always allocated correctly.
Keep records of every bet so you can see your actual profit.

blocks.text: How large a bankroll do you need?

You can start with a few hundred pounds (or your local currency equivalent), but it becomes easier with more. The funds need to be spread across many bookmakers at the same time, and a surebet requires stakes at two or three of them simultaneously. With a small bankroll you'll often lack funds in the right place.
Time is the most important factor

Arbitrage arises because bookmakers don't update their odds at the same time. This also means the opportunity closes quickly. That's why it's crucial to be notified immediately, for example via push notifications or SMS, and to have accounts ready with funds in them.
Set alerts with a minimum profit threshold so you're only interrupted by opportunities worth acting on.
Common mistakes

items: Betting on two markets that look similar but aren't identical (for example, Asian handicap versus standard handicap).
Forgetting to round stakes to whole units so it looks less automated.
Placing the first bet and discovering the second odds has dropped.
Letting winnings remain unevenly distributed, so you can't cover the next surebet.

faq.q: What's the difference between arbitrage betting and surebets?
faq.a: There's no difference. Arbitrage betting is the formal term, and surebets is what individual opportunities are commonly called.

faq.q: Can you make a living from arbitrage betting?
faq.a: A few people can, but for most it's a side income. Bookmaker restrictions and the required bankroll make it difficult to scale.

hvad-er-surebets.title: What are surebets? How guaranteed odds work
hvad-er-surebets.metaTitle: What are surebets? Complete guide to arbitrage betting
hvad-er-surebets.description: Learn what surebets are, how they occur, and how you bet on all outcomes with different bookmakers to secure a guaranteed profit.
hvad-er-surebets.intro: A surebet – also called arbitrage betting or arbing – is a combination of odds across different bookmakers where you can bet on all possible outcomes of a match and still make a profit, regardless of how it ends. It sounds too good to be true, but it's pure mathematics.

blocks.text: Why do surebets exist?

Bookmakers set their odds independently of one another. They use different models, react differently to news and want to attract bets on particular outcomes. As a result, one bookmaker might offer high odds on the home team whilst another offers high odds on the away team. When the difference becomes large enough, a surebet occurs.

Surebets typically last only minutes. As soon as bookmakers adjust their odds, the opportunity disappears. That's why it requires either many hours of manual searching or a scanner that monitors the market continuously.
How to tell if it's a surebet
You calculate the inverse value of each odds (1 divided by the odds) and add them together. If the sum is below 1, you have a surebet. The lower the sum, the greater your profit.

blocks.title: Example: tennis with two outcomes
blocks.note: The sum is below 1, so this combination is a surebet.

blocks.text: How do you split your stake?

Your stake must be divided so that the payout is the same regardless of who wins. With a total stake of 1,000 units in the example above, you place approximately 494 units on player A and approximately 506 units on player B. Both outcomes return approximately 1,037 units, meaning a profit of roughly 37 units.
You don't need to calculate this yourself. Our free sure bet calculator splits the stake automatically and shows your guaranteed profit.
What should you watch out for?

items: Odds can change whilst you're placing your bets. Place the bet with the most unstable odds first.
Check that the market is exactly the same at both bookmakers, such as whether extra time counts.
Keep funds at multiple bookmakers so you can act quickly.
Bookmakers may limit accounts that only bet on surebets. Read our guide on avoiding gubbing and account limits.

faq.q: Are surebets risk-free?
faq.a: Mathematically, the profit is guaranteed once both bets are placed at the correct odds. In practice, the risk lies in odds changing, cancelled bets or errors in the market.

faq.q: How much can you earn from surebets?
faq.a: Most surebets return between 1 and 5% of your stake. The profit comes from doing it many times, not from individual big wins.

faq.q: How do you find surebets?
faq.a: You can compare odds manually, but it's slow. A surebet scanner like BetTrackerAI monitors bookmakers that operate in your market and shows opportunities as soon as they arise.

dutching-betting.title: Dutching: how to split your stake across multiple outcomes
dutching-betting.metaTitle: Dutching betting – explanation, formula and example
dutching-betting.description: Dutching means splitting your stake across multiple outcomes so you get the same return regardless of which one wins. See the formula and an example.
dutching-betting.intro: Dutching is a betting method where you back multiple outcomes in the same event and distribute your stake so that you receive the same payout regardless of which of your selections wins. The method is particularly useful in tournaments and markets with many possible outcomes.

blocks.text: The difference between dutching and surebets

With a surebet you cover all outcomes and win regardless of the result. With dutching you only cover some of the outcomes. If one of them wins, you get the same return, but if none of them win, you lose your entire stake. Dutching is therefore not risk-free.
The formula
Calculate 1/odds for each outcome and add them together. Call the sum S. The stake on an outcome is the total stake times (1/odds) divided by S. The payout will be the total stake divided by S.

blocks.title: Example: three players in a tournament, total stake £1,000
rows: If one of the three wins
If none of the three win
blocks.note: The profit is only realised if one of your three players wins. You must judge for yourself how likely that is.

blocks.text: When does dutching make sense?

items: When you believe a few outcomes hold most of the probability, e.g. the three favourites in a tournament.
When you want to spread risk instead of backing a single outcome.
When you can get better odds at multiple bookmakers and want to distribute your stake between them.

blocks.text: Dutching is not a substitute for surebets. If you want guaranteed profit, you need to cover all outcomes at different bookmakers. The calculator shows the difference immediately.

faq.q: Is dutching the same as arbitrage betting?
faq.a: No. With arbitrage betting (surebets) you cover all outcomes and win regardless of the result. With dutching you only cover some of the outcomes and can lose your entire stake.

faq.q: Can you lose money on dutching?
faq.a: Yes. If none of the outcomes you've bet on win, you lose your entire total stake.

faq.q: How do you calculate dutching stakes?
faq.a: Add 1/odds together for your outcomes (S). The stake on each outcome is the total stake times 1/odds divided by S.

dutching-betting.ctaLabel: Use the calculator to split your stake

tennis-surebets.title: Surebets in tennis: how to find and play them
tennis-surebets.metaTitle: Tennis surebets – find guaranteed profit on tennis odds
tennis-surebets.description: Tennis is ideal for surebets because there are only two outcomes. See a worked example and the pitfalls you must avoid when arbitrage betting on tennis.
tennis-surebets.intro: Tennis is one of the easiest sports for playing surebets. A match has only two outcomes and no draw, so you only need two bookmakers and two bets.

blocks.text: Why tennis suits surebets

With two outcomes, the calculation is straightforward, and you only need to place two bets. Many matches are played every day across time zones, so bookmakers are constantly setting new odds, and they don't do it uniformly.

blocks.title: Example: odds 1.95 and 2.20, total stake £1,000
blocks.note: The sum is below 1, so the combination is a surebet.

blocks.text: Pitfalls in tennis surebets

items: Retired players: If a player retires mid-match, bookmakers' rules can differ. Some void the bet, others settle it. Read the terms at both.
Walkovers and matches that are never played can result in voided bets and an open position.
Wrong match: Check players' names and the tournament, especially in smaller tournaments where names can be similar.
Live odds change quickly. Pre-match surebets are easier to place in time.

blocks.text: Place the bet first where the odds are most volatile, then place the other afterwards. That way the risk of being left with half a surebet is minimised.

faq.q: Why is tennis good for surebets?
faq.a: Because there are only two outcomes and no draw. You only need two bookmakers and place two bets.

faq.q: What happens if a player retires mid-match in a surebet?
faq.a: It depends on the bookmakers' rules. Some void the bet if the match isn't completed, whilst others settle it. It's one of the biggest risks in tennis arbitrage betting, so read the terms first.

fodbold-surebets.title: Surebets in football: how to cover three outcomes
fodbold-surebets.metaTitle: Football surebets – how to split 1X2 odds
fodbold-surebets.description: Football has three outcomes, so a surebet requires three bets. Learn how to split your stake across home win, draw and away win, and which pitfalls to avoid.
fodbold-surebets.intro: Football has three possible outcomes: home win, draw and away win. A surebet on the 1X2 market therefore requires three bets, and the best odds are often found at three different bookmakers.

blocks.text: How to calculate three outcomes

The formula is the same as for two outcomes. Add 1/odds together for all three outcomes. If the sum is below 1, you have a surebet. The stake for each outcome is the total stake multiplied by 1/odds divided by the sum.

blocks.title: Example: three bookmakers, total stake £1,000
blocks.note: The profit is smaller than in tennis, and three bets mean a greater risk that odds will change whilst you're placing them.

blocks.text: Pitfalls in football surebets

items: Check that the market applies to the same match time at all bookmakers. 1X2 normally only covers regular time, but verify the rules for cup ties and play-off matches.
Postponed and abandoned matches are settled differently, so read the rules at each bookmaker.
Three bets create a greater risk that odds will change. Place the most volatile bet first – usually the bet with the highest odds or on the least liquid market.
Consider using two-outcome markets such as Asian handicap or over/under 2.5 goals if you want to stick to two bookmakers and reduce exposure to odds shifts.

blocks.text: Select the bookmakers where you already have funds in BetTrackerAI, so you only see surebets you can actually place.

faq.q: Why are football surebets harder than tennis surebets?
faq.a: Because there are three outcomes instead of two. You need to place three bets, often at three different bookmakers, and the risk of odds changing whilst you place them is greater.

faq.q: Does the 1X2 market include extra time?
faq.a: Normally not. 1X2 generally only covers the 90 minutes plus stoppage time, but rules may vary. Always check the terms and conditions at each bookmaker before placing your bets.

bookmakerens-margin.title: Bookmaker's margin: how to see what odds really cost
bookmakerens-margin.metaTitle: Bookmaker's margin – calculate overround and find better odds
bookmakerens-margin.description: Bookmakers profit from a built-in margin in their odds. Learn to calculate it and find the bookmakers that give you the best odds.
bookmakerens-margin.intro: When you add up the implied probabilities from a market, the total comes to more than 100%. The excess is the bookmaker's margin, also called overround. It's the price you pay to bet.

blocks.text: How to calculate the margin
Calculate 1/odds for all outcomes in the market and add them together. Subtract 1 from the total and you have the margin.

blocks.title: Example: football match with odds 2.10, 3.40 and 3.60
blocks.note: Odds of 2.10 equate to 47.6%, but without the margin the true probability is approximately 45.4%.

blocks.text: Why does the margin matter?

The lower the margin, the better odds you get for the same probability. Over many bets, the difference between 3% and 7% makes a significant difference to your bankroll. So compare margins at the bookmakers you use on the markets you bet most.
Margin and surebets

A surebet arises when the best odds from multiple bookmakers together give a total below 1. The bookmakers' margin is then more than offset by their disagreement on price. That's what a scanner looks for.
Use our calculator to enter odds and see the total straight away. If it's below 1, you have a surebet.

faq.q: What is a good bookmaker margin?
faq.a: The lower, the better. On popular football markets a margin of 3–6% is typical, and smaller leagues and specialist markets often have higher margins.

faq.q: What is overround?
faq.a: Overround is the English term for the bookmaker's margin, i.e. how much the implied probabilities add up to over 100%.

asiatisk-handicap.title: Asian Handicap Explained: Whole, Half and Quarter Lines
asiatisk-handicap.metaTitle: Asian Handicap Explained – Simple Guide with Examples
asiatisk-handicap.description: Understand Asian handicap: what -0.5, -1 and -0.25 mean, when you get your stake back, and why the line matters when placing surebets.
asiatisk-handicap.intro: Asian handicap is a football betting market where the draw is eliminated or split. This creates just two outcomes, which is why it's often used by those looking for surebets and arbitrage betting opportunities.

blocks.text: Whole lines: stake returned on draw

With a handicap of 0 or a whole number, your stake can be returned. Home team 0 means you get your money back if the match ends in a draw. Home team -1 means the team must win by at least two goals to return a profit. If they win by exactly one goal, you get your stake back.
Half lines: no stake returned
At -0.5, the team must win. A draw or loss results in a lost bet. At +0.5, you win if the team wins or draws. It's always either a win or a loss, and the stake is never returned.
Quarter lines: stake split in two
At -0.25, the stake is split in two: half on 0 and half on -0.5. At +0.25, it's half on 0 and half on +0.5. The result can therefore be a half win or a half loss.

blocks.title: Home team -0.25 with £100 stake
blocks.note: With +0.25 on the away team, it's reversed: a draw gives a win on one half and the stake back on the other.

blocks.text: Asian handicap and surebets

Because the market has two outcomes, you can combine home team -0.5 at one bookmaker with away team +0.5 at another and only need two bookmakers for a surebet. Make sure both sides have the corresponding line: -0.5 pairs with +0.5, and -0.25 pairs with +0.25.
Always check the line before placing a surebet. A difference of a quarter line can turn a guaranteed win into a risky bet.

faq.q: What does Asian handicap -0.5 mean?
faq.a: The team must win the match to return a profit. A draw or loss results in a lost bet.

faq.q: Do I get my stake back with Asian handicap?
faq.a: With whole lines, such as 0 or -1, you get your stake back if the match result exactly matches the handicap. With half lines this never happens, and with quarter lines you can get a half win or half loss.

bet-tracker.title: Bet tracker: how to keep track of your bets
bet-tracker.metaTitle: Bet tracker – track your bets, profit and ROI (2025)
bet-tracker.description: What is a bet tracker, and why do you need one? Learn what to record and how to see your true betting profit.
bet-tracker.intro: A bet tracker is a record of your bets. It shows how much you've staked, how much you've won, and which bookmakers are holding your money. Without a record, you don't know whether you're actually making money.

blocks.text: Why you need to track your bets

Most punters remember their big wins and forget the many small losses. A bet tracker removes the guesswork. You see your results as they really are, and you can see which sports, markets and bookmakers are delivering a profit.

For sure bets, it's even more important. Each sure bet consists of two or three bets placed with different bookmakers, and the profit is often only a few per cent. One misplaced bet can wipe out the profit from several sure bets, and you'll only spot that if you record everything.
What you need to record for each bet

items: Date and match
Bookmaker
Market and outcome, e.g. over 2.5 goals
Odds and stake
Result: won, lost or void
For sure bets: which bets belong together, so you can see the profit for the entire combination

blocks.text: Spreadsheet or bet tracker?

A spreadsheet works, but it requires discipline, and it won't automatically give you an overview of your balance with each bookmaker. A dedicated bet tracker calculates profit, ROI and bankroll for you, and it shows your progress over time in a graph.
BetTrackerAI has a built-in tracker where you record sure bets and deposits, and see profit, ROI and balance per bookmaker. You can also import a bet slip instead of typing it in.
How to get started

items: Record your current balances with each bookmaker as a starting point.
Record each bet as soon as you've placed it, not afterwards.
Update the result when the match finishes.
Review your tracker each week and notice what's working.

faq.q: What is a bet tracker?
faq.a: A bet tracker is a tool that records your bets and calculates your profit, ROI and balance, so you know exactly how you're doing.

faq.q: Do I need to track sure bets differently from ordinary bets?
faq.a: Yes. A sure bet consists of several bets that belong together. Record them as one combination so you see the overall profit and not a loss on the leg that didn't come in.

roi-betting.title: ROI on betting: how to calculate your return
roi-betting.metaTitle: ROI Betting – How to Calculate Return on Your Bets
roi-betting.description: Learn to calculate ROI and yield on betting with examples. See what a good return is, and why ROI tells you more than your total profit.
roi-betting.intro: ROI stands for return on investment and shows how many per cent you earn relative to what you've staked. It's the figure that tells you whether your strategy works, regardless of how large your stakes are.

blocks.text: The formula
ROI = profit divided by total stake, multiplied by 100. Profit is what you've been paid out, minus what you've staked.

blocks.title: Example: a month of sure bets
blocks.note: You've earned 2.5p for every pound you've staked.

blocks.text: ROI and yield are the same thing

In betting, the terms ROI and yield are often used for the same figure: profit relative to total stake. Some instead calculate ROI relative to your bankroll. That gives a higher figure, because the same bankroll is used many times over. Always check which method a figure has been calculated with before comparing.
What is a good ROI?

items: Ordinary bets in the long term: most punters sit below 0%, because the bookmaker takes a margin.
Value betting: 2–5% over many bets is a good result.
Sure bets: typically 1–5% per sure bet, but almost without risk, because all outcomes are covered.

blocks.text: ROI is most meaningful over many bets. After 20 bets, the figure can swing a lot. After several hundred bets, it shows whether your strategy holds up.

faq.q: How do I calculate ROI on betting?
faq.a: Take your profit, divide by your total stake and multiply by 100. If you've staked £10,000 and earned £300, your ROI is 3%.

faq.q: What's the difference between ROI and profit?
faq.a: Profit is the amount you've earned. ROI is profit as a percentage of your stake. It makes it possible to compare results with different stakes.

faq.q: Can I see my ROI automatically?
faq.a: Yes. The accounts in BetTrackerAI calculate your ROI based on the bets you record.

betting-regnskab.title: Betting accounts: how to keep track of your bankroll
betting-regnskab.metaTitle: Betting Accounts – Track Your Balance Across Bookmakers
betting-regnskab.description: Learn how to keep accounts for your betting: deposits, withdrawals and balance at each bookmaker. Never lose track when betting across multiple sites.
betting-regnskab.intro: When you place sure bets, you have money sitting with many bookmakers at once. A betting account shows you where your money is and how much you've earned when you add it all together.

blocks.text: Why you lose track

With arbitrage betting you win at one bookmaker and lose at another. Your balance is constantly shifting, and you need to deposit and withdraw regularly to have money in the right places. Without proper accounts, it's hard to see whether you're up overall.
What your accounts should include

items: All deposits and withdrawals at each bookmaker
Your current balance at each bookmaker
All bets with stake, odds and result
Your total profit: current balances plus withdrawals minus deposits

blocks.text: Good habits for bankroll management

items: Record deposits and withdrawals the same day.
Reconcile your balance with the bookmaker's own balance once a week.
Keep your betting money separate from your everyday money, so you don't accidentally bet with money you need for other things.
